papers.title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
papers.abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

papers.title: Largest-Angle Bisection and Statistical Regularization of Triangle Shapes
papers.abstract: Largest-angle bisection (LAB) repeatedly divides a triangle by bisecting its largest angle. Although this procedure is known to preserve nondegenerate triangle shapes, less is known about the distribution of shapes across the resulting refinement tree. We show that its long-term behavior is governed by a distinction between pure and mixed branches. A branch that eventually selects only one of the two children may approach an exceptional family of shapes. By contrast, every branch that changes children infinitely often converges in shape to a right-isosceles triangle. This follows from a projective Lyapunov function that is non-increasing at every refinement and decreases strictly whenever the selected child changes. Consequently, a random branch converges to the right-isosceles shape with probability one, and the proportion of triangles near that shape tends to one across complete refinement levels. Largest-angle bisection therefore produces statistical regularization even though exceptional branches remain present.

papers.title: Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
papers.abstract: Phase locking in oscillator networks depends critically on the interaction strengths between coupled units. In many applications, however, these couplings are uncertain, state dependent, or time varying. We derive rigorous conditions for phase locking in Kuramoto-type networks when each coupling strength is known only within prescribed bounds. Building on a convex formulation of the nonlinear fixed-point equations, we obtain edge-wise error bounds for arbitrary feasible approximations that hold uniformly over all admissible couplings. These bounds yield sufficient conditions for the existence of phase-locked states with prescribed phase-difference limits. We illustrate the framework for AC power grids with uncertain voltage magnitudes and adaptive oscillator networks with state-dependent couplings. For the latter, the bounds can be further tightened by exploiting the state dependence of the couplings.

papers.title: PCF All The Way Down
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.

papers.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
papers.abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational $\alpha$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $n\alpha$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.

papers.title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
papers.abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

papers.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
papers.abstract: We study the Lebesgue measure of wandering continua and related invariant sets in Julia sets, using the hyperbolic area method recently developed by Ye. For entire functions of finite type, we show that a wandering continuum of positive area must escape to infinity uniformly. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we show that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.

papers.title: Accessibility of collapsed Anosov flow
papers.abstract: We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.

papers.title: Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
papers.abstract: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Br\'evard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.

papers.title: Dolgopyat estimate for partially hyperbolic systems: limit theorems and exponential mixing
papers.abstract: We prove a Dolgopyat-type estimate for the twisted transfer operators of a class of two-dimensional partially hyperbolic endomorphisms of the torus, not necessarily skew-products. The twist satisfies a quantitative transversality condition on the cotangent dynamics of the associated three-dimensional extension which, in the skew-product case, is related to Tsujii's notions of transversality and partial captivity conditions. We use the main estimate to prove higher order expansions in the central and mixing local limit theorems for the two-dimensional base, including the case of several ergodic absolutely continuous invariant measures, and we prove exponential decay of correlations for the associated three-dimensional circle extensions, with a partially hyperbolic base.

papers.title: Exponential Deviations and H\"older Continuity for Moving-Law Mixed Cocycles
papers.abstract: We study mixed random-quasiperiodic cocycles whose one-step laws evolve along an ergodic environment. Under mixed-base ergodicity, bounded logarithmic growth, and stationary-value uniqueness, which we characterize by relative quasi-irreducibility, we prove exponential quenched deviations for finite-time directional growth. A renewal example shows that, in general ergodic environments, annealed exponential deviations can fail despite quenched exponential concentration. This obstruction motivates us to consider a fixed finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov environment, where we establish annealed exponential deviation estimates uniform over a relative neighborhood of a reference sampling kernel in the bounded mixed-base-ergodic class at each fixed tolerance. These estimates yield local H\"older continuity of the maximal Lyapunov exponent near a stationary-value-unique kernel with a simple top exponent. Under common matrix and inverse bounds, the continuity applies to synchronized Wasserstein perturbations with fixed translation marginals and continuous matrix fields, or to ordinary Wasserstein perturbations with uniform H\"older regularity in the phase. As an application, suitable frequency-support and noise-nondegeneracy conditions yield H\"older energy dependence for moving-law Schr\"odinger cocycles with continuous potentials.

papers.title: Planar Central Configurations of Four Equal Masses: Classification and Morse Indices
papers.abstract: We study the planar central configurations of four equal positive masses under homogeneous interactions with force exponent $A>2$. For $2<A\le 3$, we prove that there are exactly four types of configurations up to similarity and relabeling: the square, the centered equilateral triangle, a unique nontrivial concave kite, and a unique collinear configuration. Combined with known results for $A>3$, this completes the classification for all $A>2$ and gives an affirmative answer to Problem 11 of Albouy, Cabral, and Santos. We also establish the nondegeneracy modulo rotation of these configurations and determine their Morse indices, confirming Hampton's Conjecture 2. Our proofs are based on analytic arguments and exact algebraic calculations.

papers.title: Natural Expansiveness and Equilibrium States for Semiflows
papers.abstract: We introduce natural expansiveness, a notion of expansiveness for non-invertible dynamical systems which is defined by using the natural extension. We show that every expansive homeomorphism or flow, every positive expansive endomorphism and every positive expansive semiflow without end points is naturally expansive. Moreover, we prove that the suspension of a naturally expansive endomorphism is naturally expansive. This gives examples of naturally expansive semiflows which are neither positive expansive nor restrictions of expansive flows. Then we extend natural expansiveness and the topological pressure to semiflows which are not necessarily continuous, by using a pseudosemimetric $d_\rho$. We introduce the notion of $d_\rho$-conjugacy, and we prove that every regular impulsive semiflow is $d_\rho$-conjugate to a continuous semiflow. As an application, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of equilibrium states for regular impulsive semiflows.

papers.title: Delay-induced multirhythmicity in a 3-cell inhibitory network
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of a delayed three-cell central pattern generator network using return-map analysis and a phase-reduced description derived from generalized FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators. The phase model captures the emergence and stability of synchronous, pacemaker, and traveling-wave rhythms and provides a systematic, computationally efficient framework for characterizing the network dynamics beyond direct return-map calculations. We conduct extensive two-parameter analyses of both the full and phase-reduced models, revealing rich multi-rhythmic dynamics and transitions among coexisting rhythmic states. The close agreement between the two descriptions establishes phase reduction as an efficient and reliable framework for characterizing the dynamical organization of delayed neural oscillator networks.

papers.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
papers.abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.

papers.title: $\omega$-limit sets of triangular maps over periodic orbits of the base
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f(x),g(x,y))$ be a continuous triangular map of the unit square and let $z=(x_0,y_0)$ be a point such that $\omega_f(x_0)$ is a periodic orbit $\{p_0,\dots,p_{m-1}\}$ of $f$. Then $\omega_F(z)=\bigcup_{i}\{p_i\}\times M_i$ for nonempty compact sets $M_i$, and we ask which $m$-tuples $(M_0,\dots,M_{m-1})$ occur. For $m=1$ the answer is a theorem of Kolyada and Snoha. We show that a tuple occurs if and only if there are continuous surjections $M_i\to M_{i+1}$, indices modulo $m$, whose composition around the cycle is chain transitive. This is a cyclic version of classical facts due to Dowker and Friedlander, Sharkovsky, Hirsch, Smith and Zhao, and Kolyada and Snoha. It yields two necessary conditions: no $M_i$ is one of the exceptional sets of Kolyada and Snoha, and there are continuous surjections $M_0\to M_1\to\dots\to M_{m-1}\to M_0$. We prove that these conditions are also sufficient when every $M_i$ has uncountably many connected components, and when every $M_i$ has countably many components of which only finitely many are nondegenerate. In particular the sections of one $\omega$-limit set need not be homeomorphic. Every tuple satisfying the two conditions falls into one of these cases or into a single remaining class, in which the sections have countably many components and infinitely many of them are nondegenerate; that class is studied in a companion paper.

papers.title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
papers.abstract: We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis. We also consider two discrete-time sequences of occupation measures, induced by the algorithmic time scale and the iteration count, respectively, and we establish their almost sure convergence to the same invariant measure in the $2$-Wasserstein distance. We then derive corresponding convergence rates in expectation, providing a nonasymptotic complement to the almost sure results. These expectation bounds also imply some tail probability estimates. Finally, we verify that our results apply to a canonical class of linear recursions.

papers.title: A comparison of three models of a whirling string as it becomes chaotic
papers.abstract: A stretched wire driven near its fundamental frequency can leave the plane of the driving force and whirl. At larger amplitudes the whirl becomes modulated, reverses its direction, and becomes chaotic. Three models of this motion are in common use: the geometrically exact string equations; a two-mode model -- the Kirchhoff-Carrier equation with one transverse mode in each plane; and the averaged equations for the slow amplitudes of those two modes. We integrate all three under similar conditions and compare them along the route to chaos, which starts with a Hopf bifurcation of the steady whirl and passes through period doublings to chaotic attractors organized by a Shil'nikov homoclinic orbit. The small parameter of the averaging, the ratio $\varepsilon = c/\omega_1$ of the modulation rate to the fundamental frequency, runs from 0.005 to 0.02. Qualitatively the three models agree in the sequence of bifurcations, the coexisting attractors, the return maps and the Lyapunov exponents. Quantitatively, averaging places each local bifurcation $0.7\varepsilon$ to $1.2\varepsilon$ higher in the scaled detuning. The geometrically exact and two-mode models agree with each other to within 0.002 at the local bifurcations for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$. The Shil'nikov ratio, which decides whether chaos accompanies the homoclinic orbit, agrees among the three models to within 1.5% for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$, yet the homoclinic bifurcation itself moves by about $\varepsilon$ at the lower damping and by 6 to 9 times $\varepsilon$ at the higher; the difference is set by how quickly the return of the homoclinic loop changes with detuning.

papers.title: Time-Averages along Partial Orbits for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate the convergence of time-averages of continuous functions along partial orbits for continuous dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Unlike the classical focus of ergodic theory on convergence almost everywhere, our study emphasizes convergence at every point, motivated by problems in number theory. To this end, we consider a sequence having a uniform behavior property in the natural numbers. We also define and study two structural properties of dynamical systems along such partial orbits: minimal mean Lyapunov stability and minimal mean attractability. Our main result shows that if a continuous dynamical system is both minimally mean Lyapunov stable and minimally mean attractable along a given uniformly behaved sequence, and is minimally uniquely ergodic, then the time-average of any continuous function along the corresponding partial orbit converges to the space average at every point.

papers.title: Koopman Generator Decomposition for Port-Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian energy balance and Koopman approximation describe different aspects of nonlinear dynamics. This paper distinguishes exact observable identities, measure-dependent Galerkin projections, constrained surrogate identification, and certification of a controller on the nonlinear plant. Conservative weak skewness requires compatible measure and boundary conditions. Dissipative positivity belongs to the metric bracket; it does not generally make the projected first-order dissipative derivation positive. We give an explicit fixed-metric compatibility condition and a constant--Hamiltonian dictionary obstruction, and state the assumptions under which surrogate certificates imply plant bounds. A reproduced pendulum experiment illustrates the practical gap: its learned controller admits an exact shaped-energy certificate on the nonlinear plant, although its fitted quadratic storage is not a plant Lyapunov function and its archived residual-norm diagnostic is uninformative. These conclusions use the specified plant structure; they are not generic finite-data guarantees. The bracket, projection, and Lyapunov arguments are positioned relative to existing structured identification and residual-aware control methods.

papers.title: Spectral clustering of time-evolving networks using spatio-temporal random walks
papers.abstract: Temporal (or time-evolving) networks provide a natural framework for modeling complex systems with time-dependent interactions, where understanding the evolution of community structures is a central challenge. While random walk-based approaches to community detection in static networks are well established through the spectral analysis of associated transfer operators, extending these ideas to temporal networks is nontrivial due to the inherent time-dependence of the underlying dynamics. In this work, we develop a general framework for community detection in temporal networks that is based on multi-view canonical correlation analysis (mCCA). We show that the proposed formulation admits a spectral characterization via a time-reversible random walk on an augmented space-time network, providing a clear dynamical interpretation of temporal communities as metastable structures of the process. Furthermore, we analyze key spectral properties of the resulting transfer operators and the interplay between spatial and temporal effects, which allows us to distinguish between structural features and artifacts induced by the snapshot coupling. Finally, we derive a reduced-order model, which preserves the essential spectral properties while significantly improving computational efficiency. We show that the proposed approach effectively detects communities in temporal networks and captures their evolution.

papers.title: Metric mean dimension of flows
papers.abstract: We introduce metric mean dimension to characterize the complexity of continuous flows with infinite topological entropy and derive some of their elementary properties. The main results of this paper are as follows: $(1)$ We prove that different types of measure-theoretic $\epsilon$-entropies of ergodic measures have the same divergent rate, and establish analogous variational principles for metric mean dimension in terms of the measure-theoretic $\epsilon$-entropies of continuous flows. $(2)$ We introduce the measure-theoretic metric mean dimension of invariant measures and link it to metric mean dimension via a classical-type variational principle. $(3)$ Using the Carath\'eodory-Pesin structure, we introduce Bowen metric mean dimension on subsets and establish the variational principle for Bowen metric mean dimension of any non-empty compact subset. Furthermore, we show that the Bowen metric mean dimension of the set of generic points of an ergodic measure is bounded by the divergent rate of the upper and lower Brin-Katok $\epsilon$-entropies.

papers.title: Ergodicity of a surgered flow on unit tangent bundle of hyperbolic surface
papers.abstract: Starting with a trivial periodic flow on $\mathbb{S}M$, the unit tangent bundle of a genus two surface, we perform a Dehn-type surgery on the manifold around a tubular neighborhood of a curve on $\mathbb{S}M$ that projects to a self-intersecting closed geodesic on $M$, to get a surgered flow which restricted to the surgery region is ergodic with respect to the volume measure. The surgered flow projects to a map on the surgery track that can be taken to be a linked twist map with oppositely oriented shears which generates the ergodic behavior for sufficiently strong shears in the surgery.

papers.title: Observable Dynamics and the Generic Coincidence of Milnor, Statistical, and Physical Attractors
papers.abstract: We study observable dynamics of generic continuous interval maps. We prove that, for a residual subset of $C([0,1])$, the global Milnor, statistical, and physical attractors coincide with the non-wandering set. Thus, for a typical interval map, the asymptotic dynamics detected by Lebesgue-almost every initial condition recovers all recurrent dynamics. The common attractor is a robust Cantor set of zero Hausdorff dimension. Moreover, every invariant probability measure has a basin of zero Lebesgue measure. We also present examples showing that, outside the generic setting, positive topological entropy may occur outside the global Milnor attractor, and the three attractors need not coincide.

papers.title: Existence of the Lyapunov exponent for $S$-unimodal maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for any $S$-unimodal map $T$ on $[0,1]$ with a non-flat critical point the Lyapunov exponent exists for Lebesgue almost every point and is equal to a constant $\lambda_T$. Moreover, $\lambda_T=0$ if and only if $T$ admits neither an absolutely continuous $T$-invariant probability measure with positive entropy nor a strictly stable periodic orbit. Consequently, if an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point is infinitely renormalizable or non-statistical then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ exists and is equal to $0$. A key ingredient is the following result of independent interest. If an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point has no periodic attractor then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the lower Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ is non-negative. This shows that, in the absence of periodic attractors, exponential contraction cannot occur along the orbit of Lebesgue almost every point.

papers.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
papers.abstract: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:\mu(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto \mu(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.

papers.title: Strong Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness of parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem using strong stable manifolds and direct action comparisons. Fix a minimal normalized central configuration $c$, with no nondegeneracy assumption. In McGehee coordinates, every parabolic motion with this limiting configuration has a tail on the outgoing strong stable manifold. Its local graph yields a smooth velocity field on a truncated cone, selecting a collision-free parabolic motion that stays in the cone and is unique among all such cone-confined motions. For free-time minimizing rays, an explicit renormalized action excess gives a no-exit estimate, hence uniqueness from a smaller cone without a confinement assumption. Together with known existence results, these cone theorems imply that every $c$-parabolic motion has a tail that is a $c$-parabolic geodesic ray. Globally, we propagate the stable graph backward and compare the excess on its regular branches. An endpoint differential formula and Sard's theorem imply that the configurations admitting more than one such minimizing ray form a Lebesgue-null set. The uniqueness proofs combine local dynamics and variational comparisons without using differentiability of a global Hamilton--Jacobi solution.

papers.title: Hyperbolic scattering in the planar $n$-body problem with homogeneous strong force potentials
papers.abstract: For the planar $n$-body problem with homogeneous strong force potentials, given an arbitrary pair of normalized collision-free configurations $(a, b)$, we prove that for any positive energy $h$, there are infinitely many $h$-energy scattering orbits between $a$ and $b$.
